sentences.text: Many individual investors use free web tools such as Google Finance to look up stock and fund prices.
Google Sheets includes a built-in function that pulls stock and fund prices into a spreadsheet.
That price data can be used to graph and compare securities over a chosen time period.
Quotes for bonds are harder for individual investors to find than quotes for stocks or mutual funds.
Compulsive spending is often a psychological issue rather than purely a money problem.
Seeing a counselor or therapist early can help address the underlying compulsion before it worsens.
Any plan to reduce overspending works best when both spouses agree to it together rather than one dictating to the other.
Couples should agree on a monthly budget without using it as a tool to control the other spouse.
When one partner spends compulsively, keeping separate bank accounts with a joint account for shared bills like the mortgage can help.
An underwriting discount is the fee the investment bank earns for selling a company's IPO shares, built into the offering price.
In a normal trade, the buyer pays a commission to the broker on top of the share price.
In an IPO, the seller usually pays the commission, so the buyer pays only the offering price.
The underwriting bank typically buys the shares wholesale from the company and then resells them to the public.
For US IPOs, the underwriting discount commonly runs around 7% of the offering proceeds.
A lender cannot refuse to provide you with your current balance or a balance history.
Under US truth-in-lending laws, a lender is obligated to furnish a copy of the finance contract on request.
You should make your request in writing so the company's response is documented.
Sending the letter by certified delivery and keeping copies helps if the dispute later goes to court.
If the dealer still refuses, you can file a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau or your state attorney general.
Most Americans with private coverage get health insurance through their employer.
Employer-sponsored premiums can be paid with pre-tax dollars if the employer sets the plan up correctly.
Self-employed people can deduct health insurance premiums on Form 1040, but only for months they are not eligible for an employer-subsidized plan.
Arrangements where an employer simply passes premium money through to employees are relatively uncommon and are restricted by ACA rules.
Wealthbot is an open source wealth management platform aimed mainly at registered investment advisors managing multiple portfolios.
Wealthbot includes features such as rebalancing, portfolio accounting, and tax-loss harvesting.
Stock Portfolio Manager is an open source project for tracking a personal stock portfolio.
Lists of open source software often include a financial section with additional portfolio tools.
Paychecks in the US are generally considered stale after six months, and banks may decline to cash them.
The employer still owes you the wages even if the check itself has expired.
You should contact the employer's payroll department and ask them to reissue the check.
If the employer has turned the funds over to the state, you can claim them through your state's unclaimed property office.
A non-EU business selling digital services to UK customers must register for VAT if its sales exceed the UK registration threshold.
VAT should have been charged at the time of sale rather than months later.
UK and EU rules require prices shown to consumers to include applicable taxes.
A US-based seller may argue those display rules do not apply to it.
Since the price you agreed to was presumably VAT-inclusive, you generally have no obligation to pay an extra VAT charge after the fact.
Not all Visa cards are tied to a bank account.
Visa debit cards draw funds directly from the cardholder's bank account.
Visa credit cards bill the cardholder rather than withdrawing money from an account at the time of purchase.
Prepaid cards only allow spending up to the amount already loaded onto the card.
Some banks let you link a Visa credit card to a chequing account to pay off the balance automatically each month.
Stock trades in the US settled on a T+3 basis at the time, meaning cash from a sale arrives three business days later.
You cannot withdraw sale proceeds until they settle.
In a margin account, regulations permit trading with unsettled funds right away.
In a cash account, buying and then selling a security before paying for it with settled funds can trigger a good faith or free-riding violation.
Brokers set their own rules, so some allow more trading with unsettled cash than others.
There is no single salary at which AMT kicks in, because it depends heavily on your deductions as well as your income.
For 2015, the AMT exemption was $53,600 for single filers and $83,400 for married couples filing jointly.
Taxpayers with income above the exemption who claim large deductions and pay little regular tax are the most likely to owe AMT.
Exercising incentive stock options can trigger AMT even for people with moderate salaries.
Since the 2017 tax law raised the exemption and phase-out thresholds, AMT mostly affects households earning several hundred thousand dollars a year.
In the US, news reports about interest rates are usually referring to the federal funds rate set by the Federal Reserve.
Changes in the federal funds rate ripple through to other interest rates in the economy.
The Fed's FOMC meets eight times a year to set its target for the federal funds rate.
Some people instead mean the prime rate, which banks charge their most creditworthy customers.
Others may be looking at long-term rates such as mortgage or Treasury yields, which can move differently from short-term rates.
Exchange rates are driven by supply and demand for each currency.
For large amounts, a bank wire or a specialist currency transfer service usually offers better rates than airport or retail exchange counters.
Comparing the offered rate with the mid-market rate shows how much spread you are paying.
Once you convert, you are exposed to future movements in the exchange rate.
Some investors spread a large conversion over several transactions to reduce the risk of exchanging at a bad moment.
Bond prices move inversely to yields, so when yields rise, the bond's price falls.
A bond's price equals the present value of its future coupon and principal payments, discounted at the yield to maturity.
To get the new price, you recompute that present value using the new, higher yield.
Modified duration gives a quick approximation: the percentage price change is roughly minus the duration times the change in yield.
For example, a bond with a modified duration of 5 would fall about 5% in price if its yield rose by 1 percentage point.
The full set of outstanding limit orders for a security at a point in time is called the order book.
The best bid is the highest buy order and the best ask is the lowest sell order.
Standard quotes show only the top of the book, meaning the best bid and best ask.
Deeper order-book data, known as Level 2 market depth, is available through many brokerage platforms and exchange data feeds, often for a fee.
For a sole proprietor, Solo 401k contributions, whether employee or employer, are deducted from gross income rather than reducing it at the wage level.
For an S-Corp owner, employer contributions are excluded from W-2 wages, so they do reduce gross income.
A sole proprietor can make employer profit-sharing contributions of up to 20% of net self-employment earnings.
Solo 401k contribution limits are based on self-employment income rather than total income.
Sole proprietors claim the employer contribution as an adjustment to income on Form 1040 rather than as a business expense on Schedule C.
A true 0% loan is a losing proposition for the bank on its own.
Interest-free loans often include late payment fees, prepayment penalties, or other clauses that make them profitable on average.
Banks look to profit across thousands of loans rather than on each individual loan.
Retailers offering 0% financing typically bake the financing cost into the sale price.
Because the loan is secured, the bank can seize the collateral if the borrower defaults, which keeps its risk low.
A self-directed IRA lets you invest in virtually anything that counts as an investment.
This flexibility is valuable if your expertise lies in an asset class that typical brokerages do not offer.
Custodian fees for self-directed IRAs can be high, so it pays to compare custodians.
Being more hands-on also means more responsibility for avoiding prohibited transactions, which can disqualify the IRA.
Gold has historically been used to preserve value and hedge against inflation.
Gold-backed ETFs such as GLD let you gain exposure to gold without storing it yourself.
Some argue that paper gold like GLD may offer less protection than physical gold during severe inflation.
Gold's inflation-hedging role plays out over long periods, and its price can spike for other reasons in the short term.
Gold produces no income, so it is better viewed as a store of value than as a productive investment.
It is legal for an F-1 student to invest in stocks, including foreign markets.
F-1 students are typically treated as nonresident aliens for tax purposes during their first five calendar years in the US.
Nonresident aliens file Form 1040NR rather than Form 1040.
Some US-based brokers, such as Interactive Brokers, let you buy shares directly on foreign exchanges.
You should account for dividends and capital gains when filing your US taxes, and student tax software may not handle this well.
Historical option prices are available for many listed options, though usually not for free.
OptionMetrics is one commercial provider of historical option data.
OptionMetrics data is drawn from the National Best Bid and Offer.
Some brokerage platforms also let customers view historical charts for option contracts they are researching.
Yes, a mortgage is a loan, so you are technically in debt while you are paying it off.
Many people distinguish mortgage debt from consumer debt and treat it as acceptable borrowing.
All debt costs money in interest, so the key question is whether the benefit of borrowing is worth the cost.
A mortgage is secured by your house, so defaulting on it can lead to losing your home.
Common financial advice treats being debt free except for a regular mortgage as a reasonable milestone.
A stockbroker arranges the buying and selling of stock for clients by matching buyers and sellers.
A broker does not purchase the stock for himself but simply arranges the trade.
A trader buys stock with the hope of selling it later at a gain.
Traders typically use a broker to execute their purchases and sales.
Becoming a stockbroker requires a license, while being hired as a trader generally requires a proven track record of making money.
Landlords are mainly looking to exchange space for regular, drama-free rent payments.
Screening tenants for sufficient income or assets helps reduce the risk of missed rent.
In Michigan, a landlord must deposit a tenant's security deposit with a regulated financial institution or secure it with a bond.
Michigan law does not require landlords to pay interest on security deposits.
Landlords dealing with difficult tenants should follow state landlord-tenant law closely and document everything in writing.
Credit bureaus such as Equifax collect personal data about individuals and score their creditworthiness.
Consumers generally cannot opt out of having credit bureaus collect their data.
The 2017 Equifax breach exposed enough personal data to enable large-scale identity fraud.
In the US, you can opt out of prescreened credit offers by calling 1-888-5-OPT-OUT or visiting optoutprescreen.com.
Placing a free credit freeze with each bureau prevents new credit from being opened using your file.
The foreign exchange market works much like the stock market, with buyers bidding and sellers asking for one currency in terms of another.
Like stocks, currencies also trade through swaps, futures, and options.
Currencies rise and fall based on supply and demand.
A fiat currency's value is influenced by the state of the country's economy and its government's fiscal policies.
Interest rate differentials set by central banks are also a major driver of currency movements.
Shares of a privately held company are not traded on a stock exchange.
To buy or sell private company stock, you generally need to deal directly with the company or its current owners.
Many private companies have shareholder agreements that give the company or other shareholders a right of first refusal on any sale.
Some secondary marketplaces, such as Forge Global or EquityZen, match sellers of private company shares with accredited investors.
The basic rule is to compare your loan's interest rate with the return you expect from investing.
If the interest on the debt is higher than your investment returns, paying off the debt is the better investment.
If your loan rate is very low, such as under 1%, investing the money may come out ahead if you can earn more than that rate.
Paying down debt gives a guaranteed return equal to the interest rate, while investment returns are uncertain.
High-interest debt like credit cards should generally be paid off before lower-rate debt like a mortgage.
In the US, gains on stocks and ETFs are taxed as capital gains when you sell.
Long-term gains on stocks and stock ETFs are typically taxed at 15% for most investors.
Precious metal ETFs such as IAU are taxed as collectibles at up to 28%.
The wash sale rule disallows a loss if you buy the same stock within 30 days before or after selling it at a loss.
ETFs tend to be more tax-efficient than mutual funds because they distribute fewer capital gains.
A financial institution asking for a member breakdown usually wants to see the LLC's operating agreement.
The operating agreement should state that the LLC is a single-member entity and that the sole member holds 100% ownership and all managerial authority.
Every LLC is required to have an operating agreement, even though it usually does not have to be filed with the state.
For federal tax purposes, a single-member LLC is typically a disregarded entity reported on the owner's personal return.
Taking time to research charities before giving helps ensure your donation goes where it will have the most impact.
Charity evaluators such as GiveWell and Charity Navigator rate organizations on effectiveness and financial transparency.
Setting up a charitable trust lets you spread donations out over years or decades.
In the UK, a Charities Aid Foundation account lets you donate anonymously while the charity still benefits from Gift Aid.
Donating to large name-brand charities can result in more solicitations because some charities share donor information.
Small businesses can deduct ordinary and necessary business expenses from taxable income.
When an item like a phone is used for both business and personal purposes, only the business portion is deductible.
Keeping itemized bills and receipts is important to support the amount you deduct.
Tax deductions are designed to create economic incentives, such as encouraging charitable giving that benefits the community.
In Canada, a lower corporate tax rate applies to income eligible for the small business deduction, up to the business limit.
Generally, you owe income tax in the country where you physically perform the work, which in this case is France.
A non-US person living outside the US and doing contract work for a US company generally does not pay US income tax on that income.
If the US employer withholds tax anyway, you may need to claim a refund from the IRS.
US citizens and green card holders are taxed on worldwide income regardless of where they live.
Americans living abroad can usually offset US tax with foreign tax credits or the foreign earned income exclusion, but must still file US returns every year.
The main reason to put 20% down on a home is to avoid paying private mortgage insurance (PMI).
Many advisors recommend against putting more than 20% down so you keep cash available for emergencies and other investments.
Extra money beyond 20% can go toward retirement savings or an emergency fund instead.
You can always make extra mortgage payments later, but you cannot easily get money back out of the house.
A common rule of thumb is that the mortgage payment, including property tax, should be no more than 28% of gross monthly income.
Claiming your father as a tax dependent should not by itself make him ineligible for SNAP.
SNAP groups people into one household if they live together and purchase and prepare meals together.
If your father lives separately and buys his own food, he would generally be treated as his own household.
SNAP eligibility depends on the household's income and countable resources such as bank accounts.
The IRS does not coordinate dependency claims with SNAP, which is administered by a separate agency.
You cannot transfer stock you already own in a taxable account directly into a Roth IRA.
Roth IRA contributions must be made in cash, so you would need to sell the stock and contribute the proceeds.
Annual Roth IRA contributions are capped, at $5,500 at the time of the passage.
Selling the stock to fund the contribution may trigger capital gains tax.
Existing Roth IRA assets can be moved between custodians in kind through a transfer handled by the new custodian.
Selling a stock at a loss and buying it back within 30 days triggers the wash sale rule, which disallows the loss.
Selling a stock at a gain and repurchasing it, known as tax-gain harvesting, can reset your cost basis higher.
Holding a stock for more than a year qualifies gains for lower long-term capital gains rates.
High earners may also owe the Net Investment Income Tax on capital gains.
Investors sometimes sell worthless stock simply to realize a loss for tax purposes.
The best source of a company's financial statements is usually the investor relations section of its website.
For US public companies, annual financial statements are in the 10-K filing and quarterly ones are in the 10-Q.
These filings are available for free on the SEC's EDGAR database.
Finance pages of Google, Yahoo, and MSN provide normalized balance sheets and income statements.
For Canadian companies, the SEDAR database compiles official financial statements.
Yes, ScholarShare is California's official state-sponsored 529 college savings plan.
California does not offer a state income tax deduction for 529 plan contributions.
Because there is no state deduction, California residents can choose another state's plan if its fees or options are better.
Comparing annual fees is an important step before choosing any 529 plan.
A bond's value is the present value of its expected future cash flows.
The yield to maturity serves as the discount rate applied to those cash flows.
To price a bond to yield X%, you discount each coupon payment and the face value at X% and add them up.
This approach is based on time value of money principles.
If the coupon rate is higher than the yield, the bond will be priced above its face value.
